chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who said:

I was staying in Al-Madina during the month of Ramadan in the year two hundred and thirteen. So when Eid al-Fitr approached, I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about whether going out for an Umrah during the month of Ramadan is superior, or staying until the month ends and I complete my fasting. He wrote to me a letter which I read in his own handwriting: 'You asked, may Allah have mercy on you, which Umrah is superior? An Umrah during the month of Ramadan is superior. May Allah have mercy on you.'
ai.seo_question: Is Umrah in Ramadan better than fasting?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Ali ibn Hadeed queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the comparative merit of performing Umrah during Ramadan versus remaining to complete the month's fasting. The Imam’s concise reply, 'Umrah in Ramadan is superior,' establishes a key principle in Shia jurisprudence that the spiritual reward of Umrah in Ramadan rivals or exceeds that of a Hajj, thereby prioritizing the pilgrimage over the mere continuation of fasting. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the cumulative virtues of combining acts of worship during the holy month.
